\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{booktabs}
\title{Plant Community Assembly Along an Elevation Gradient
in the Hengduan Mountains}
\author{Y.~Cheng, R.~Alvarado, and P.~Nilsen}
\date{April 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
We surveyed vascular plant communities at eight sites spanning 2,050 m
of elevation in the Hengduan Mountains.
Species richness declined monotonically with elevation, while the
proportion of clonal species increased.
Community turnover was best explained by the interaction of temperature
seasonality and soil phosphorus.
Our results support a shift from competitive to facilitative structuring
above 3,300 m.
\end{abstract}
\section{Introduction}
Elevation gradients compress the climatic range of an entire latitudinal
belt into a few kilometres, making them natural laboratories for the
study of community assembly.
In the Hengduan Mountains of southwest China, rapid uplift and complex
topography have produced one of the richest temperate floras on Earth.
Yet quantitative surveys that link community structure to measured
environmental gradients remain scarce for the region.
Here we ask three questions.
How does species richness change along the elevation gradient?
Does the relative importance of deterministic and stochastic assembly
processes shift with elevation?
And which environmental variables best explain compositional turnover
among sites?
\section{Study Area and Methods}
The study area lies on the western flank of the Yulong massif.
Eight sampling sites were established between 1,830 and 3,880 m,
spaced at roughly equal elevational intervals.
At each site we laid out five 20 m by 20 m plots and recorded all
vascular plant species, their cover, and twelve soil and microclimate
variables.
Sampling was carried out in the growing seasons of 2023 and 2024.
The eight sampling sites are summarized in Table \ref{tab:sites}.
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{Sampling sites along the elevation gradient.}
\label{tab:sites}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Site & Elevation (m) & Annual precipitation (mm) \\
\midrule
S1 & 1830 & 1042 \\
S2 & 2140 & 1118 \\
S3 & 2460 & 1203 \\
S4 & 2790 & 1187 \\
S5 & 3050 & 1094 \\
S6 & 3320 & 1008 \\
S7 & 3610 & 946 \\
S8 & 3880 & 902 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
Species nomenclature follows the regional flora.
Clonal growth was scored from field observation and trait databases.
We used variation partitioning to separate the contributions of
climate, soil, and spatial structure to compositional turnover.
\section{Results}
We recorded 214 vascular plant species across the eight sites.
Species richness per plot declined from 48 at the lowest site to 11
at the highest.
The proportion of clonal species increased from 22 percent at low
elevation to 61 percent at the highest site.
Turnover between adjacent sites was highest between 3,050 and 3,320 m,
coinciding with the treeline ecotone.
Variation partitioning attributed 41 percent of the compositional
variance to the joint effect of temperature seasonality and soil
phosphorus, while pure spatial structure explained 9 percent.
Table \ref{tab:turnover} reports the pairwise turnover summary.
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{Pairwise compositional turnover (Bray--Curtis) between
adjacent sites.}
\label{tab:turnover}
\begin{tabular}{lc}
\toprule
Site pair & Turnover \\
\midrule
S1--S2 & 0.42 \\
S2--S3 & 0.47 \\
S3--S4 & 0.44 \\
S4--S5 & 0.51 \\
S5--S6 & 0.63 \\
S6--S7 & 0.58 \\
S7--S8 & 0.55 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\section{Discussion}
The monotonic decline in richness mirrors patterns reported from
other Asian massifs, but the increase in clonality is stronger than
published averages for temperate gradients.
We interpret this as evidence that facilitative interactions and
vegetative persistence increasingly structure communities near the
upper distributional limit of vascular plants.
Two limitations qualify these results.
First, our plots sample only the western flank, and aspect effects
remain untested.
Second, the two-year window may miss decadal shifts in recruitment.
\section{Conclusion}
Along the Hengduan elevation gradient, plant communities shift from
speciose, competitively structured assemblages to depauperate,
clonally dominated ones.
Compositional turnover peaks at the treeline, and the joint effect of
temperature seasonality and soil phosphorus dominates the explained
variance.
Future work should extend the design to the eastern flank and to
experimental warming.
\appendix
\section{Additional Tables}
Supplementary summaries of the field campaign are collected below.
The plot-level species counts underlying the richness analysis are
given in Table \ref{tab:richness}.
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{Recorded species richness per plot at each site.}
\label{tab:richness}
\begin{tabular}{lc}
\toprule
Site & Mean species per plot \\
\midrule
S1 & 48 \\
S2 & 43 \\
S3 & 37 \\
S4 & 31 \\
S5 & 24 \\
S6 & 17 \\
S7 & 13 \\
S8 & 11 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\end{document}
